newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 to 5.00 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 3.00 to 5.00 higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 3.00 to 5.00 cents higher Tuesday as dealers expect the market to bounce back from Monday's weak finish.

Traders also said the London market's recovery from session lows overnight buoyed sentiment. Robusta futures were still weaker early Tuesday, in quiet trading led by the ring. At the midday break, benchmark LIFFE September was down $12 at $1,833 a tonne after sinking to a low of $1,790.

Monday, New York arabica futures ended broadly lower in choppy dealings. September settled down 4.05 cents at 175.45 cents a lb after ranging from 185.00 to 170.00. Spot July finished 4.30 lower at 194.65, with the outer months down 5.10 to 6.00.
The July/September switch narrowed to 19.20 cents from 19.45 cents at the close Friday.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 185.00 cents, with the next upside target at 192.00 to 194.00 cents. Support was seen at September's low of 168.75 cents which was set last week.
On the weather front, no damaging cold is expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday.
There may be some disruptions and delays to the Brazil harvest due to very wet weather this month, WSC added.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 900 60-kg bags as of June 20, to 46,425 bags. There were 3,100 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Also after Monday's close, CSCE said it will lower the margin on the July "C" coffee contract by $1,000, to $9,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, effective today.
The margins on all other coffee contracts will remain unchanged, the exchange said in a statement.
